newsitem.title: USA: Virginia expands use of commercial paper.
newsitem.headline: Virginia expands use of commercial paper.

text.p: Virginia is expanding its use of commercial paper to secure short-term financing ahead of longer bond issues, state Treasurer Susan Dewey said Wednesday.

The state began a pilot program last fall, issuing commercial paper with maturities ranging from one day to 270 days. The short-term debt is used to finance construction start-up costs at lower interest rates, enabling the state to fine-tune issue size and timing for long-term bond issues for state projects.
"We see a significant advantage. It helps us when we issue long term bonds to know better how much we will need for a certain period of time," Dewey said in a telephone interview.

"We believe that overall the savings for financing a project would be about nine basis points, based on the pilot program," she said. "We've been very pleased. I think we're one of the first states actually taking advantage of this."

The state previously was authorized to issue $50 million of commercial paper in conjunction with general obligation bonds. Another $25 million GO authorization has been added, along with a $25 million authorization for revenue bonds, Dewey said.
"That's just our own self-imposed limit at this point. It could be expanded if we see the need," she said.

The authorization for revenue bond projects will allow Virginia Public Building Authority, College Building Authority and Commonwealth Transportation Board to use commercial paper for their bond-financed projects, Dewey said.
Goldman, Sachs & Co was chosen last year to underwrite the debt and its contract continues through the spring of 1997.
